chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fudalah from Husayn ibn 'Uthman from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥalabī said:

I asked him about wearing khazz (silk), and he said, 'There is no harm in it. Indeed, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to wear a khazz cloak in winter. When summer came, he would sell it and give its price in charity, and he would say, 'I shy away from my Lord from eating the price of a garment in which I worshipped God.'

key_terms.اَلْخَزِّ: Khazz (fine silk), a type of silk fabric
key_terms.عَلِيَّ بْنَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ: Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS), the fourth Imam

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for men to wear silk according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *khazz* (fine silk) for men by citing the practice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), who wore it in winter and sold it in summer. The ethical nuance lies in his statement about not 'eating' the price of a garment used for comfort/worship, reflecting a Shia juristic view that distinguishes between the utility of the item and the accumulation of wealth from its sale, thereby avoiding spiritual attachment or misuse of the proceeds.
